description:
From the fz-kdt.106 cold review (2026-09-01). Vec<Ty>::equivalent is
pointwise Types::is_equivalent = mutual is_subtype, and is_subtype
decides closure-arrow emptiness from fn_id + captures alone
(emptiness.rs::func_clause_empty ~:191-219 -- args/ret never read), so a
template arrow and a ground arrow over ONE lambda are judged equivalent.
Consequence AT BASE, today: a template row and a ground row whose other
columns match already collapse into each other in
ActivationInputAlternatives::insert_row, and which one survives is
whichever ARRIVED FIRST -- a pre-existing schedule-confluence hole in the
correlated-input antichain. Measured (review harness, equiv_not_dom
counter): 8 fixtures exhibit pairs equivalence accepts that the kdt.106
dominance relation rejects -- 52 on 00277, 46 on behavior/enum_map_family,
30 on range_map, 16 on 00420, 8 on 00276, 6 each on
list_literal_trailing_call and map_enumerable.

DECIDE: either the equivalence skip adopts the same
free-var-set/literal-shape discipline as Types::row_column_dominates and
the two fold into ONE relation (preferred -- fold-concordant), or
insert_row documents why two contradictory judgements about one pair
coexist and which is authoritative. fz-kdt.106's build documents the
coexistence; this ticket owns the fold decision and its artifact
re-measurement.
title: insert_row's whole-row equivalence skip is closure-literal-blind: arrival order decides which of a template/ground pair survives at base
